title: Parameterization beats escaping
prompt:
Implement two functions that contrast safe and unsafe query building:

- `build_query(template, params)` — the parameterized world. The template may contain `?` placeholders; values are rendered with `repr()` (a quote in a value stays a literal quote inside a quoted token, never changing statement structure). Placeholder-count mismatch raises `UnsafeQuery('placeholder count mismatch')`. Returns `(rendered, 'parameterized')`.
- `vulnerable_query(template, values)` — the string-formatting world. Render with `template.format(*values)`; if the result contains `drop table` (case-insensitive), `' or '1'='1`, or a `;`, raise `UnsafeQuery('injection detected in string-built query')`; otherwise return it.
- define `class UnsafeQuery(Exception)`.

The discriminating scenario: `O'Brien` as a customer name must flow safely through `build_query` unchanged (quotes preserved) — while the same string in the vulnerable path is a hand-escaping hazard.

tests.name: legit data survives parameterization intact
tests.hint: repr() keeps the value literal; structure never changes.

tests.name: the vulnerable path is caught red-handed
tests.hint: String-formatting + payloads = flagged; plain values pass through.
